import re from typing import List # Regular expression to match simple HTML tags. # It looks for a '<', then any characters that are not '>' (non-greedy), and ends with '>'. _TAG_RE = re.compile(r'<[^>]+?>') def identify_html_tags(content: str) -> List[str]: """ Scan the given HTML string for tags and return a list of all detected tags. Parameters ---------- content : str The HTML string to parse. Returns ------- List[str] A list of matched tag strings, e.g. ['
', '']. The list preserves the order of appearance in `content`. Notes ----- - The function is intentionally conservative: it does not attempt to validate tag syntax or handle malformed input. It simply captures any sequence that starts with '<' and ends with the next '>'. - The regex is deliberately simple to avoid catastrophic backtracking (CWE-407). It uses a non-greedy match that stops at the first '>' after '<', ensuring linear complexity in the length of `content`. - Any exception raised during matching is caught and results in an empty list, guaranteeing that the function never propagates errors. """ if not isinstance(content, str): return [] try: # Find all non-overlapping matches of the pattern. return _TAG_RE.findall(content) except Exception: # In case of any unexpected error, return an empty list. return []
